case_notes.func_value_map: R1 misses the call because `h("a b")` calls a function value taken from a map; the naive graph only follows calls written by name. VTA tracks the value `vulnlib.Parse` into the map and out to `h`, and reports a DYNAMIC edge main -> Parse. This is the failure that motivated ADR-002/004.
case_notes.reflect_method: The disagreement the CP2 spec predicts. VTA reports NO_PATH: the call goes through `reflect.Value.Call` on a method found by a run-time name, and x/tools documents VTA as sound only 'modulo use of reflection and unsafe' (go/callgraph/vta/vta.go). The linker keeps `Impl.Run` and therefore `Parse`: once a reflect method lookup is reachable, the linker's dead-code pass (`reflectSeen` in cmd/link/internal/ld/deadcode.go) keeps exported methods of reachable types. NO_PATH + PRESENT gives CANT_DETERMINE / METHOD_DISAGREEMENT. VTA alone would have been a false NOT_REACHABLE; this is why the rule needs the second method. R1 also misses it (no call written by name).
case_notes.interface_not_instantiated: R1 is a false REACHABLE: the naive graph links the interface call `r.Run` to every method named `Run` in the analysed packages, including `worker.Run`, which no value ever reaches. VTA sees that only `quiet{}` flows to `r`.
case_notes.method_value: R1 misses the call: `f := vulnlib.Impl{}.Run; f("a b")` calls a method value, not a name. VTA follows it through the bound-method wrapper `Impl.Run$bound`.
case_notes.build_tag_excluded: VTA and naive both return TARGET_NOT_FOUND because `vtfixtures/vulnlib` is imported only by `tagged.go`, which the default build excludes, so the package is not in the loaded program. The contract says a symbol absent from the loaded program must not become NO_PATH, so the combined verdict is CANT_DETERMINE / ANALYSIS_FAILED. This is safe (truth is NOT_REACHABLE) but costs an answer. Proposed design change, not implemented: let the helper report 'target package not imported by the program' separately from 'symbol not found in a loaded package', so the verdict rule can decide whether the former may count as NO_PATH (it is only safe if the target package path itself is known to be correct).
case_notes.generic_call: R1 misses the call: `viaGeneric[string]` is passed to `apply` as a function value and called there. VTA follows the value and reports a DYNAMIC edge `apply[string] -> viaGeneric[string]`.
case_notes.unsafe_func_pointer: VTA reports NO_PATH (a false NOT_REACHABLE for VTA alone): the function value passes through an `unsafe.Pointer` conversion, and VTA does not track types through `unsafe` (documented limit, see reflect_method). The linker keeps `Parse` because its value is taken. So, contrary to the CP1 note, this case does exercise `unsafe` — for call-graph methods, not for the linker. The combined verdict is CANT_DETERMINE / METHOD_DISAGREEMENT, not a false NOT_REACHABLE.
case_notes.generic_target: VTA supports the generic form: the target `ParseAny[T]` matches the instance `ParseAny[string]` and a path is found. The linker still returns UNSUPPORTED_SYMBOL_FORM (no verified rule for generic binary names), so the combined verdict is CANT_DETERMINE / ANALYSIS_FAILED. A verified linker rule for generic instances would let this case be answered.
case_notes.present_but_unreachable: The case CP1's review asked for. The linker keeps `loud.Run`, and so `Parse`: `loud` is converted to an interface (stored in `any`), and a method with the same name and signature is called from a reachable interface call site (`r.Run`), which is the linker's rule for keeping methods of types used in interfaces (`ifaceMethod` / `markableMethods` in cmd/link/internal/ld/deadcode.go). VTA sees that only `quiet{}` reaches `r`. NO_PATH + PRESENT gives CANT_DETERMINE / METHOD_DISAGREEMENT. Linker presence alone is a false REACHABLE; R1 is too (name match on `Run`).
case_notes.closure_never_called: The linker keeps `Parse` because the closure that calls it is created and stored, so its code is in the binary even though it never runs. VTA has no edge to the closure, because nothing calls `stored`. CANT_DETERMINE / METHOD_DISAGREEMENT. R1 attributes calls inside function literals to the enclosing function (main), so it is a false REACHABLE.
case_notes.method_expression: R1 misses the call: the method expression `vulnlib.Impl.Run` is assigned to `f` and called through it. VTA follows it through the thunk `Impl.Run$thunk`.
case_notes.interface_two_impls_one_used: R1 is a false REACHABLE through the name match on `Run` (it links `r.Run` to `vulnlib.Impl.Run`). The linker drops `Impl.Run`: the type assertion `r.(vulnlib.Impl)` alone did not keep the method (observed; the linker internals for this were not traced). VTA and linker agree on NOT_REACHABLE.
case_notes.first_construction_devirtualized: Not a case id. In the first version of `present_but_unreachable` and `interface_two_impls_one_used`, `r` was assigned directly in main (`var r runner = quiet{}`). The compiler devirtualized `r.Run` (`go build -gcflags='-l -m'` printed `devirtualizing r.Run to quiet` / `to echo`), so no interface call reached the linker and it dropped `loud.Run`: linker ABSENT, no disagreement. Both cases now get `r` from a constructor, which keeps the interface call. Truth did not change. The linker result for a present-but-unreachable symbol therefore depends on compiler optimisations, which matters for real applications.
case_notes.synthetic_call_sites: Not a case id. Edges inside compiler-generated package initialisers (for example `init_imported.init -> initdep.init -> initdep.init#1`) have no source position; the helper reports them with call_site file "" and line 0. The CP7 verifier will need a rule for these edges.
